skillSays: Work in two steps: first write a short design philosophy (a named visual movement, 4-6 paragraphs), then express it on a canvas as 90% visual design and 10% essential text.
Deduce a subtle, niche reference from the request and weave it into the form and colour, like a jazz musician quoting another tune, instead of drawing the subject literally.
Treat the piece like a plate from a scientific atlas: dense accumulation of repeated marks, systematic reference markers, sparse clinical typography, a limited and intentional palette.
Text is minimal and thin by default, set in distinctive fonts; nothing overlaps, nothing leaves the canvas, everything has margin.
Emphasise master-level craftsmanship, then do a final refinement pass that polishes what is there rather than adding more graphics.

changes: Movement 'Nocturne Instrumentation': the jazz subject is never drawn. The reference is civil twilight, with ~700 dots on concentric rings about a sun marked at -6 degrees below a ticked horizon.
A single five-line staff holds a blues phrase whose flat 3rd, 5th and 7th notes are amber, the only warm accent on the plate.
Title in thin, wide Jura Light spaced to the full measure, supported by tiny DM Mono plate labels and one line of italic serif.
Refinement pass removed labels that touched the arcs and tuned dot size and colour by ring so the sky fades from amber to indigo.
Movement 'Kinetic Ledger': the subtle reference is 42.195 km. About 420 straight pace lines, one per runner, fan from a single start point to their finish times on a distance-time plate.
Only the front group and the last 195 metres are vermillion; everyone else is fine grey ink, so the colour says who leads.
Context allowed a bolder type gesture than the thin default: a huge condensed 42.195 in Big Shoulders with mono axis labels.
Final pass shrank the chart so the numeral no longer touched the time axis and kept all text inside the frame.

Movement 'Cartographic Strata': the map theme is carried by a 512-line portolan rhumb network (black, green and red as on real portolan charts) from 16 points around a hidden circle, with a land mass drawn as water-lining echoes.
A row of four tiny plates generated in code - T-O map, conic, Mercator and orthographic graticule - tells the history as a quiet sequence instead of text.
Thin Italiana title with Crimson Pro italic and Plex Mono labels, on parchment with oxblood and verdigris as the only accents.
Refinement removed a compass N that collided with the header and moved the plates up so captions clear the title.
